requirement:
The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
in `used`, as described in {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.mcp.description`.
rationale:
The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]` covers each obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions`. I judged this from the test text alone and did not read the implementation.

- **First result carries `instructions`, even when empty.** In the first conversation (`session`), the first successful delivery is a `search_text` for "absent" with no matches. The test parses `instructions` from it and requires it to be a string.
- **Text and structural searches share the rule.** A separate conversation (`peer`) makes `search_structure` its first search. Its `matches` is `[]`, and `page["instructions"]` equals the earlier instructions. The `session` and `fresh` conversations use `search_text`.
- **Each conversation gets its own instructions.** `fresh` and `peer` are separate `SessionTools` instances. Each has its own first delivery, and each carries the same `instructions`. The `fresh` first result `hits` is compared with `instructions`.
- **Failed searches do not use up the instructions.** Before any success, `session` runs `search_text` with the invalid pattern `(`, and the test asserts that it errors. The next, successful search still carries `instructions`.
- **Later searches omit the field.** The later `peer` `search_text` has no `instructions`. The later `session` `search_text` for "hit" has none either, and neither does the page fetched by `get_next_page` after the changed file.
- **Continuation pages omit the field.** `rest` from `get_next_page` in `fresh` has no `instructions`, and `second` in `session` has none.
- **Content explains when to call `finish_search` and which tags go in `used`.** The test asserts these phrases in the instructions: "Before submitting, close every delivered search page", "finish_search", "tags for excerpts you relied on without a separate source read", "used:[] if none qualify, including an empty result", and "without reading more source". Together they cover when to call and which tags to include. The separate `instructions.content` requirement is also marked on this test.

Small untested variations: a failed structural search is not tried before the first success, and the second search in `fresh` (`capped`) is not checked for an absent `instructions`. Neither is a named obligation. The failure rule is stated generically and exercised through a failed text search. Omission on later searches is asserted elsewhere in the test.

The cited `finish_search.mcp.description` requirement is context only, and I did not reassess it.

text: The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
> `Close a delivered search and record dependencies for snippets you used to
> justify your conclusion without an additional source read. search_id is the
> result's UUID and used is an array of its short entry tags, e.g.
> whose source you also read may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use
> used:[] when no entries qualify, including an empty search. Every delivered
> search must be finished before submission. The result is {search_id,
> finished:true}; no additional source is delivered.`
